newsitem.title: CANADA: Poco CEO expects no competing Gardiner bid.
newsitem.headline: Poco CEO expects no competing Gardiner bid.

text.p: Poco Petroleums Ltd does not expect a bid to surface to compete with its C$225-million takeover proposal for Gardiner Oil & Gas Ltd, Poco president and chief executive Craig Stewart said on Wednesday.
"I'd be surprised," Stewart said in an interview.
Under the friendly cash and stock deal announced late on Tuesday, 73 percent of gardiner shareholders agreed not to tender to a competing offer unless it was valued at over C$13.50 per share.
"It's a fairly onerous thing," he said. "It could happen, but, I'd be very surprised."
Poco said it would pay C$5 plus 0.6 of a Poco share for each Gardiner share.
Based on Poco's current share price of C$11.10, each Gardiner share would fetch the equivalent of C$11.66.
Stewart said Gardiner's acreage and production base, which fits with Poco's own natural gas exploration and production program, is the key to the acquisition.
"In discussions with Gardiner, they indicated that they had quite a number of approaches from other companies," he said.

"One of the principal reasons that this deal was done with Poco, and was done on obviously an exclusive basis, is that they also saw that the properties would be extremely well- managed because of the production we have in the areas."
He said Gardiner had done a good job in building its assets, which are concentrated in western Alberta, over the past few years and had decided the time had come to move them into a larger operation.
Gardiner shares jumped 2.10 early on on Wednesday to C$11.60 on turnover of 72,600. Poco was trading down 0.25 to C$11.10 on volume of 80,880.
